recipes.name: Slow Cooker Baked Beans with Ham Hock

steps.text: In a large pot over high heat, combine the beans with water to cover and bring to a boil for 10 minutes. Remove from heat but let sit for 1 hour. Drain beans and place them in a slow cooker. Add the ham hocks, onion, brown sugar, maple syrup, salt and water.

Mix well, cover and cook on high setting for 4 to 5 hours, stirring occasionally. During the final hour of cooking, add the ketchup and mustard, remove the ham from the hocks and discard the hocks. Mix well and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Baked Beans with Ham Hock
raw_recipe.description: For those who love to do it themselves, here's a terrific recipe for genuine baked beans - and it's so easy to make! Soak white beans and then pop them into your slow cooker with ham hocks, onion, brown sugar, maple syrup, ketchup and mustard.

review.reviewBody: I read all of the reviews first and went with using one 16oz package of beans. I boiled for a while and probably went over 10 mins and let them sit a little over an hour. I just took my time about it. I started the crockpot at 12:30 on High and the beans were perfect by 4:30. Right amount of sauce too and never added more water. I still stayed casual and finished the recipe with the final steps and ingreds and went another hour on low for fear I've over cook them. These are professonal, afordable, and gormet-looking and tasting! This recipe is what your teen boys will brag to their future wives about! No can will ever compare. These are a wow! I will memorize this one!

For those of you who have hard beans you may need to put 1/8 tsp of baking soda in your water when soaking (this is stated on the back of the navy bean bag for hard water or use bottle water). I was scared after reading many reviews but my beans came out soft in the amount of time stated in the recipe. I did use the quick method, used the water they boiled and sat in for an hour. I also filled my crock pot up with this water to more than cover the beans while cooking. As others stated used a can of tomato paste during the cooking process, and then at the end used some ketchup and mustard. Also used cut up pieces of country ham for the meat and a small vadilia onion. Taking to the lake today, looking forward to hearing great reviews.

This recipe is an excellent variation on baked beans with the maple syrup replacing the standard molasses. You will never need to buy another can of baked beans once you try this recipe. it can also be made changing the syrup to molasses or to a honey molasses or honey syrup mixture. it works well with the ketchup but requires more liquid if you substitute tomato paste as some have suggested. I would recommend sticking with ketchup. To insure your cooking times, it helps to stretch aluminum foil over crock then placing the lid on top. This maintains the temperature & moisture levels a little better. I added more ketchup & syrup/molasses/honey (whatever I used each time I make them) at the beginning of the time in the slow cooker. I have also added BBQ sauce for a variation. They are a complete meal with the ham (also good with browned breakfast sausage added in place of the ham!) When soaking beans over night or doing the "quick soak" method, always add baking soda to the water they are soaked in ,& do not add salt til the end of cooking. I've read this in many older cookbooks & had many elder cooks tell me this. A friend whose culture has a diet based on beans says this is how people in her country always prepare beans. The only caveat, do not use more than 1/2 tsp baking soda to the pound of dry beans or they will taste bitter in the recipe.

Good beans. As others have said, you may have to adjust timing or water as everyone's slow cooker is different. I adjusted the water a lot; I put several inches of water above the beans and then had to add more in while soaking. I did not drain the beans before putting in the slow cooker. This did make for rather soupy beans while cooking in the slow cooker, but eliminated the need to add water back in to the cooker while they were cooking away. I also waited to add the meat (I just used cooked and chopped bacon pieces) until about 4 hours into the cooking process. I didn't have maple syrup, so I used maple flavoring and honey. I'm not sure that adding salt up front means beans won't cook or not, but I prefer to add seasonings like that at the end--so hard to adjust down! So, I waited to add the salt and pepper with the mustard and ketchup at the end. I had a 2 pound, so 32 ounce, bag of pinto beans (no navy or Great Northern beans at Target) and per hubs this needed another 1/2 cup of brown sugar at the end to bring it to his preferred sweetness, as the only adjustment I made for the increased beans was the water. I did have to keep the lid off halfway for the last 1 or 2 hours of cooking to bring the liquid down. All told, we ended up with about 5 meals (there are two of us) of baked beans, so I froze three of them for another time, and it cooked for about 8 hours on high. Thanks for sharing!

I made a few tweaks to this recipe. I soaked my beans overnight, sautéed my onions first, added a can of kidney beans for fun, and cooked in my instant pot for 40 minutes. Such a great recipe!! I plan on putting in my Dutch oven and heating slowly on my smoker tomorrow.

We love these beans! I make them vegetarian (we don't generally eat pork of any sort), add a touch more water (about 1/2 a cup to a cup) and use honey instead of maple syrup though if I had molasses on hand at the time I'd do a honey-molasses mix. I also use homemade ketchup from this site. I don't soak them overnight but do the quick soak method. One thing about the quick soak method is you need much more water than "just to cover them" as this recipe suggests. Add water to at very least about 3 inches above the beans in the pot. Boil for 10 minutes and then let them sit covered and untouched for at least an hour but more if you've got the time. Another thing is stirring the beans often. Maybe two to three times an hour. This prevents some from overcooking. I use 1lb/16oz of dried beans but I leave the rest of the recipe as is. To be fair this recipe, in our opinion, is much more "mustard-y" than standard baked beans but we like that about them. All in all I give these beans 5 stars with my alterations. I give the recipe here 4 because it suggests too little water both in the quick soak and in the crock pot. HOWEVER the water amounts as written in this recipe may work for you. All crock pots are different.

I used natural maple syrup which is not thick like imitation syrups so I omitted the water. I first tested the recipe by cutting in in half and using a can of navy beans - turned out great. The second time it turns out my beans were old and did not soften (no longer had the bag to check the dried beans were within 2 years). Having made it both ways, I prefer the short cut of using store bought canned beans (and have made it that way since). I have also used precooked bacon in a fix and that worked well. This is a sweet style of baked bean (which I like) but may not appeal to those whole like a stronger tomato flavor or western kick to their beans. I enjoyed how this recipe made use of pantry staples.

This makes the best baked beans!!! I have made it several times including making it in my multi cooker using the pressure cooker function. I do not put any salt in it until the last as I have heard salt inhibits the beans from getting soft. This time I made it in the slow cooker which has a browning function. I used thick sliced bacon as I could not get hocks and browned the bacon and onion first. I have made the recipe with hocks and either way it is delicious. Thanks for this recipe and it makes me think of my grandmother every time I make them.

Made these today and they turned out really great. I have made homemade baked beans for years so soaked the beans overnight, then boiled for an hour. Slow cooker for 6 hours and they turned out great. I added the ketchup and used dry mustard both at the beginning. I added only the cup of water called for in the recipe and beans were very moist.
The colouring comes from the ketchup so it is best to add early so you get that nice brown colour.

I made it with 20 ounces of dry baby lima beans and a leftover ham bone with a fair amount of ham left on it. Boiled the bone in water for about 20 minutes before adding the dry beans, brought back up to boil for 10 minutes, then let it sit for the recommended hour. Pulled the ham bone, removed the meat, drained beans and added all to the crock pot as directed, with the ketchup and mustard for last hour. It worked really well and it tastes great. The baby limas are nice for this recipe.

I'm making these now. I used 16oz great northern beans soaked overnight and then boiled for 15_min. I added a Tbl molasses, 1 Tbl minced garlic and a cup of brewed coffee (Emeril's secret ingredient). Can't wait for these to be done. The sauce tastes great!
I used bacon instead of ham hock and added sautéed carrots and celery
No changes but I did use ham in the beans.

Just like my grandma used to make. I have searched forever gor a recipe that replicates hers. Easy to make. I doubled the recipe. Soaked the beans overnight for 12 hours. Followed all directions with the exception of added 1 extra cup of water at beginning of cooking. Glad I did. Cooked in crockpot on high for 5 hrs. I can’t wait to eat this with some cornbread!
Beans WILL NOT cook in an instant or similar device, pressure or slow. Something about the coating. I learned the hard way.
Flavor is excellent, but beans were too hard. Next time I will boil the beans until they are soft. Someone suggested letting them soak over night.

Like others I too have had problems with the beans not cooking. I boiled the beans for 1 hour yesterday, changed the water and left them to soak overnight for 12 hours, then boiled them for another 20 minutes. I put them in the slow cooker today and had them cooking on high for 6 hours. When I went to check them after 6hrs before serving for dinner the beans are still crunchy. It is now 7 hours on high and they are still crunchy. The sauce is good but they were inedible for dinner time. We ended up having to order out. I have left them to continue to cook in the hopes they will be ready for tomorrow. Have had to added more water as a results and readjust the sauce.

Good first time. Wife who is of English decent loves'm so do I. A little dry, so I added more water which seemed to do the trick. BTW my store was out of smoked pork butts, so I used smoked pork neck bones, hmm good.
Super easy, and really good!

Pretry good. My family liked them too. I am not sure if it was the type of beans (I used navy) or I didn't let them cook or boil long enough, but they were a little el dente (if that applies to beans). They weren't bad, but I'm going to try to add some juice from the pineapple brown sugar honey ham I made and let the beans slow cook for a few more hours to see if that softens them up. Good taste, though.
